newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian PM makes cabinet shuffle proposals.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian PM makes cabinet shuffle proposals.

text.p: Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri told President Hosni Mubarak of his proposals for a cabinet shuffle on Monday, sources close to the government said.
Six or seven of the 30 ministers or ministers of state are expected to leave, mostly among those responsible for public services and aspects of the economy, the sources said.

Cabinet members with the key portfolios -- Defence Minister Field Marshal Mohamed Hussein Tantawi, Foreign Minister Amr Moussa and Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi -- will probably remain in their jobs, the sources added.
Ganzouri met Mubarak for one hour at the president's office and, contrary to normal practice after such meetings, he declined to tell reporters what they talked about.
In remarks published on Saturday, Mubarak said cabinet changes were on the way but candidates would be chosen carefully to ensure a smooth succession.

"As for the expected ministerial reshuffling, the president indicated that the changes were in the offing but they must be clearly defined and precisely chosen," said the government newspaper al-Gomhuria.
"It's not possible that I appoint a minister and then discover after a couple of months that he is not suitable. Stability is key," Mubarak added.
The sources said Ganzouri and Mubarak did not make any decisions on Monday, partly because many ministers are out of the country. They may announce changes next week, they added.
Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib and Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily are in Washington for talks on redressing Egypt's large trade deficit with the United States.

Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid, who runs the government's privatisation programme, left for Abu Dhabi on Sunday. The Minister of State for Economic Affairs, Youssef Boutros-Ghali, has been in London for several days.

No new members have joined the cabinet since Ganzouri took office in January 1996 with promises of accelerated economic reform. Public Works and Water Resources Minister Abdel-Hadi Radi died last November and has not been replaced.

Ganzouri's cabinet already contained many old faces from the outgoing cabinet of Atef Sedki and some of the ministers have held the same posts since the days of President Anwar Sadat, assassinated by militant Islamists in 1981.
Political sources said in March that Ganzouri was seriously considering changes in some economic portfolios but nothing came of the rumours.
